findings.summary: Spec §1.4 requires the profile-declared seed text to be commensurate with the repo named by ALLOWED_ROOT and to let the code-local worker actually find something. The profile sets ALLOWED_ROOT=/data/code/self/agent-runtime (line 30) while SEED_CLUE instructs the worker to "read src/tick-run.ts in the ALLOWED_ROOT repo ... report the exact file path and line range". File inspection of /data/code/self/agent-runtime shows no tick-run.ts anywhere in that tree (its src/ holds run.ts, dispatch.ts, roles.ts, agent-bus.ts, ...); src/tick-run.ts belongs to this plugin repo, not to ALLOWED_ROOT. The seed therefore asserts a file that the implementer could not observe in the target repo — the §0 "invent a contract for an artifact you cannot observe" shape — and on the real machine the dispatched code-local worker is sent after a nonexistent path, so acceptance criterion 9's seeded board cannot yield the intended finding.

Acceptance criterion 6 requires the name board:agent-runs to have exactly one source of truth in the repo ("⛔ 不要再写一份字面量"). src/run-channels.ts:20 is that source and src/tick-run.ts / src/tick-inspect.ts correctly import RUNS_CHANNEL_ID, but bin/e0-regression.sh:22 hardcodes a second literal RUNS_CHANNEL_ID="board:agent-runs" for the prep list and the run record. Nothing guards the drift: the discriminative test scans only src/ (test/e0c1-board-credentials.test.ts:273-309), so if the TS constant changes, the entry would silently prepare and record a different channel than harvest/triage read. The entry already shells into vite-node for the §1.2 read, so the name could be resolved from the single TS source instead of duplicated.

The only automated check on the §1.4 seed text is `expect(e0.SEED_CLUE.length).toBeGreaterThan(20)`, which cannot distinguish a repo-relevant clue from a plausible-sounding but false one (exactly the failure in the blocker above). A check tying the clue to something verifiable under ALLOWED_ROOT would make criterion 4/9 discriminative rather than length-based.

Spec §1.1 requires the loud failure to name both the channel and the field set actually received. listChannelsAt names the channel and JSON.stringify(head_seq) (i.e. `undefined`) but never prints the observed keys of the list item, so a real-machine shape change would not be diagnosable from the error alone; getChannelHeadSeq likewise prints only the present channel_ids.

The profile header still advertises loading it directly via `bin/deep-research-loop.sh --profile e0-regression`, but §1.3 removed the fixed TICK_CHANNEL from the profile and only bin/e0-regression.sh exports the derived per-run channels. Taking the advertised path now aborts at deep-research-loop.sh:79-82 with "TICK_CHANNEL is not set".

The entry passes SEED_SOURCES as a single `--source` operand, so a profile that ever declares more than one source (comma/space separated) would be seeded as one bogus source name rather than a list, and parseSeedCliArgs would accept it silently. Splitting the profile value into repeated --source operands would keep GT-2 honest for multi-source profiles.

The production-bus read helper discards the child process stderr with 2>/dev/null, so the underlying reason for a mandatory §1.2 read failure (token unreadable, HTTP status, non-numeric head_seq) is lost; the entry then reports only its own generic REFUSING line.
